native_result.query: In what scenario did urban land use promote a specific type of plant invasion?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use promoted the invasion of non-native plants introduced UNINTENTIONALLY (via global trade/tourism; ruderal annual weeds) in the scenario of urbanized landscapes — Urban habitat and surroundings with high current (2009) urban cover at 500–1000 m buffers, resulting from post-1956 urbanization — with this type promoted specifically (presence OR up to ~2.0 per +1 SD urban, p<1e-6; NB IRR ~1.5, p<1e-4) and much more strongly than gardening/agriforest species.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected all four files (dimensions, NAs, dups, integrity). 2) Temporal trend chi-square (context only). 3) Validated progressive/regressive change vars against computed 1956–2009 urban/cropland deltas (labels found REVERSED). 4) Presence-logit and Poisson/NB count models per pathway × buffer (50/500/1000 m) with covariates (cropland, elevation, log distance road/stream, temperature, rainfall). 5) Scenario test: urban_1956 vs urban_2009 in one model. 6) Head-to-head type discrimination: per-pathway ORs, compositional share of unintentional and log(gard/unint) vs urban among the 191 invaded plots. 7) Species-level trait corroboration. 8) Phylogeny: custom Newick parser, pairwise patristic distances vs random expectation (reported equivocal). 9) Count-model validation: Poisson vs NB (LR, alpha) vs ZIP/ZINB (AIC; instability reported).

sub_hypo.text: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in sampled plots in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening-introduced plants relative to unintentionally introduced plants. The hypothesis does not specify the urban land-cover year or buffer size.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.

sub_hypo.text: In urbanized landscapes of Barcelona province, urban land use promoted invasion by unintentionally introduced non-native plants, particularly ruderal annual weeds introduced via global trade or tourism, much more strongly than gardening or agriculture/forestry introductions.
sub_hypo.context: Urban habitats and surroundings with high 2009 urban cover within 500–1000 m buffers resulting from post-1956 urbanization. Head-to-head pathway comparisons included the 191 invaded plots.
sub_hypo.relations: Higher current urban cover was positively associated with presence and counts of unintentionally introduced plants: presence odds ratios up to approximately 2.0 per one-standard-deviation increase in urban cover (p < 1e-6) and negative-binomial incidence rate ratios approximately 1.5 (p < 1e-4). This association was much stronger than for gardening or agriculture/forestry species. Models jointly assessed 1956 and 2009 urban cover and adjusted for cropland, elevation, log distance to roads and streams, temperature, and rainfall; pathway discrimination also assessed unintentional compositional share and log(gardening/unintentional) against urban cover.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Urban land use promoted the invasion of non-native plants introduced UNINTENTIONALLY (via global trade/tourism; ruderal annual weeds) in the scenario of urbanized landscapes — Urban habitat and surroundings with high current (2009) urban cover at 500–1000 m buffers, resulting from post-1956 urbanization — with this type promoted specifically (presence OR up to ~2.0 per +1 SD urban, p<1e-6; NB IRR ~1.5, p<1e-4) and much more strongly than gardening/agriforest species.
